title: Dimensionality reduction: PCA, t-SNE and UMAP

videos.script: Eight columns cannot be drawn. Two can. {{two}} This lesson makes few columns out of many, for three different reasons. {{three}} To look at the customers. To feed a model less. To remove columns that repeat each other. {{reasons}} PCA keeps the directions along which the customers spread most, and its axes can be read. {{pca}} It also notices that one of the eight columns was never really there. {{seventh}} t-SNE and UMAP bend the space to keep neighbours together, and draw far better pictures. {{pictures}} Then the warnings. Distances on those pictures mean little, and t-SNE cannot place a new customer at all. {{warnings}} By the end, you know which map answers which question, and when a model is better off without one. {{end}}
